title: console-backend: Audit Logs API (list/filter + export token) w/ admin RBAC + rate limits
author: Chloe Martin
description: Implements the Console backend endpoints for Audit Logs: (1) list/query with filtering + cursor pagination and (2) export token issuance for the Console UI export flow. This is the backend piece for DES-133 and unblocks enterprise beta requirements around SIEM/export workflows. Endpoints are admin-only by default (and support explicit permissions where present in the RBAC bundle) and are protected with per-actor + per-org rate limits. The list endpoint returns schema-v1 shaped events (envelope) and enforces strict query constraints (bounded time range, max page size, allowlisted filters) to protect the audit-log query backend. Includes OpenAPI updates, request/response validation, and tests for RBAC, filter correctness, and rate limiting. API surface: GET /console/v1/audit-logs (filters: start_time, end_time, event_name[], actor_id, actor_type, target_type, target_id, outcome, request_id; sort=desc by occurred_at; pagination via cursor + limit) and POST /console/v1/audit-logs/export-token (returns short-lived token for initiating export; permission audit_logs.export required; logs internal access attempts and failures). Notes: export-token is not a direct download link; it is an authorization step used by the UI to request an export job from the exporter/exports service (keeps secrets out of the browser and centralizes RBAC). Follow-ups: wire UI, add per-customer retention/redaction messaging, and add integration coverage in the audit log E2E harness once staging exporter endpoints are stable.
commits: console-backend/auditlogs: add query model + filter parsing and validation
console-backend/http: add RBAC guards for audit_logs.read and audit_logs.export
console-backend/ratelimit: add route-level limits + metrics tags
tests: add handler tests + RBAC matrix + rate limit tests
implementation_notes: Data path: console-backend queries the audit-log query service (backed by the audit pipeline store) and maps results into schema-v1 envelope fields expected by the UI. Query constraints: end_time required; max lookback 90d; max window size 31d per request; limit default=50, max=200; cursor is opaque; sort fixed to occurred_at desc. RBAC: default-deny; requires org-scoped permission audit_logs.read for GET and audit_logs.export for POST; additionally requires org role admin unless an explicit permission grant is present (supports future role customization). Rate limits: GET /audit-logs: 60 rpm per actor + 600 rpm per org; POST /export-token: 10 rpm per actor + 60 rpm per org. Security logging: emits a structured security log line on every export-token issuance attempt (success/failure), including org_id, actor_id, request_id, and reason codes (no sensitive payload).
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng): Can we confirm that only admins can hit this, and that we don’t accidentally allow any workspace member to enumerate audit events? Also want an explicit limit on time range per request.

Chloe Martin (Author): Yup. Added default-deny permission check (audit_logs.read/export) AND an admin gate unless explicit permission is present. Also added max window size (31d) and max lookback (90d). Tests updated to cover non-admin denial.
Allison Grant (Observability): Please add request_id propagation into downstream calls + metrics per route. Also ensure we’re not emitting PII in logs when validation fails.

Chloe Martin (Author): Added request_id header passthrough to query service and route metrics (redwood_console_auditlogs_requests_total + latency histogram). Validation error logs now include only field names + reason codes, no raw values.
Nadia Rahman (Telemetry): Mapping to schema v1 looks good. One nit: outcome should be required and normalized to {success,failure,unknown} for older records; UI expects the field present.
Chloe Martin (Author): Implemented normalization in mapper_schema_v1.ts; outcome always set. Added tests for legacy records missing outcome.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/RBAC): Rate limits: can we make export-token lower and add an explicit audit for export token issuance attempts? This will show up in customer evidence.

Chloe Martin (Author): Export-token set to 10 rpm per actor. Added structured security log for issuance attempts (success/failure). We can add an audit event for export token issuance itself in a follow-up once the sensitive-actions inventory confirms naming/ownership; for now it’s server-side security logging only.
Sahana Iyer (CI/Policy): Please add a small RBAC matrix test that asserts both permissions and admin gate behavior, so future refactors don’t weaken it.

Chloe Martin (Author): Added test cases covering: admin allowed, non-admin denied, explicit permission allowed (non-admin), missing permission denied. Also added regression test that workspace members can’t access org audit logs.
release_notes: Console backend now supports Audit Logs list/filter endpoint and export-token issuance with strict RBAC and rate limits (enterprise beta prerequisite).
